concept.title: Uniqueness of Totally Disjoint Diametral Paths in Trees
concept.concept_description: For any tree, the maximum size of a set of totally disjoint diametral paths is exactly 1. That is, no tree can contain two totally disjoint diametral paths. The proof relies on the fact that if two such paths P1 and P2 of length d existed, the unique path Q connecting them in the tree would have length c >= 1. Let a and b be the distances from the respective endpoints of P1 and P2 to the endpoints of Q along P1 and P2. The distance between the far endpoints of P1 and P2 would be a + c + (d - b) <= d and the distance between the other far endpoints would be (d - a) + c + b <= d. Summing these inequalities yields 2d + 2c <= 2d, implying c <= 0, which contradicts the total disjointedness of P1 and P2.
concept.mathematical_framing: For any tree, the maximum size of a set of totally disjoint diametral paths is exactly 1. That is, no tree can contain two totally disjoint diametral paths. The proof relies on the fact that if two such paths P1 and P2 of length d existed, the unique path Q connecting them in the tree would have length c >= 1. Let a and b be the distances from the respective endpoints of P1 and P2 to the endpoints of Q along P1 and P2. The distance between the far endpoints of P1 and P2 would be a + c + (d - b) <= d and the distance between the other far endpoints would be (d - a) + c + b <= d. Summing these inequalities yields 2d + 2c <= 2d, implying c <= 0, which contradicts the total disjointedness of P1 and P2.
concept.lean_guess: By contradiction. Assume two totally disjoint diametral paths P1 and P2 of length d exist in a tree. Let Q be the unique path in the tree connecting P1 and P2, of length c >= 1 (since they share no vertices). Let a and b be the distances from the endpoints of P1 and P2 to the endpoints of Q. The distance between the far endpoints of P1 and P2 is a + c + (d - b), which must be <= d. The distance between the other far endpoints is (d - a) + c + b, which must also be <= d. Summing these yields 2d + 2c <= 2d, so c <= 0, contradicting c >= 1.

concept.title: Dimension of Second Clique Homology for Latin Square Graphs
concept.concept_description: For any Latin square M of order n ≥ 5, the dimension of the second homology group of the clique complex of the strongly regular graph associated with M over any field F is exactly (n-1)^3 - I(M), where I(M) is the number of intercalates (2x2 Latin subsquares) in M.
concept.mathematical_framing: For any Latin square M of order n ≥ 5, the dimension of the second homology group of the clique complex of the strongly regular graph associated with M over any field F is exactly (n-1)^3 - I(M), where I(M) is the number of intercalates (2x2 Latin subsquares) in M.
concept.lean_guess: Construct the clique complex of the Latin square graph, characterize the boundary maps for the simplicial chain complex, and evaluate the rank of the second homology group by establishing a bijection between the independent 2-cycles and the intercalates of the Latin square.

concept.title: Generalized scalar factor for mixed modified Greaves‑Jing‑Zhu operators
concept.concept_description: We conjecture that for any deformation parameters t and s the mixed product of the modified Greaves‑Jing‑Zhu operators yields a scalar factor that can be expressed as a rational function of infinite q‑Pochhammer symbols: F(t,s;u) = (u;t)_\u221e (‑u;s)_\u221e / ((‑u;t)_\u221e (u;s)_\u221e). Moreover, the q‑expansion of F(t,s;u) has palindromic coefficients and satisfies a finite‑order linear recurrence; after removing the alternating signs the coefficients are non‑negative integers.
concept.mathematical_framing: We conjecture that for any deformation parameters t and s the mixed product of the modified Greaves‑Jing‑Zhu operators yields a scalar factor that can be expressed as a rational function of infinite q‑Pochhammer symbols: F(t,s;u) = (u;t)_\u221e (‑u;s)_\u221e / ((‑u;t)_\u221e (u;s)_\u221e). Moreover, the q‑expansion of F(t,s;u) has palindromic coefficients and satisfies a finite‑order linear recurrence; after removing the alternating signs the coefficients are non‑negative integers.
concept.lean_guess: The conjecture can be approached by first expressing the mixed product via the diagonal conjugation that relates the modified operator to the classical neutral operator. Using known product formulas for neutral operators and Bailey‑pair theory, one can reduce the mixed product to a ratio of infinite q‑Pochhammer symbols as stated. The resulting rational function is then analyzed via standard q‑series techniques (e.g., the pentagonal number theorem) to extract its q‑expansion, prove palindromicity and derive a finite‑order recurrence. The non‑negativity of the sign‑adjusted coefficients follows from known positivity results for principal specializations of one‑row Schur Q‑functions and can be formalized using Lean’s algebraic number theory libraries.

concept.concept_description: Let p be a prime, b an integer ≥ 2 such that p does not divide b. If the multiplicative order of b modulo p is (p-1)/2, and p ≡ 1 mod 4, then the sum of the digits of one period of the base-b expansion of 1/p is (b-1)(p-1)/4.

concept.title: Polynomiality of Nilpotent Matrix Counts with Prescribed Support
concept.concept_description: For any partition λ of n and any support pattern S ⊆ [n] × [n], the number of n × n nilpotent matrices over F_q with Jordan canonical form type λ and support contained in S is a polynomial in q with non-negative integer coefficients. This extends known polynomiality results for Hessenberg supports (connected to chromatic quasisymmetric function evaluations via Shareshian–Wachs theory) and directly addresses the polynomiality questions the paper raises for more general support patterns and prescribed affine slices of adjoint orbits.
concept.mathematical_framing: For any partition λ of n and any support pattern S ⊆ [n] × [n], the number of n × n nilpotent matrices over F_q with Jordan canonical form type λ and support contained in S is a polynomial in q with non-negative integer coefficients. This extends known polynomiality results for Hessenberg supports (connected to chromatic quasisymmetric function evaluations via Shareshian–Wachs theory) and directly addresses the polynomiality questions the paper raises for more general support patterns and prescribed affine slices of adjoint orbits.
concept.lean_guess: Leverage the paper's Hall scalar product formula expressing the count in terms of skew modified Hall-Littlewood functions and q-Whittaker functions. For Hessenberg supports, connect to chromatic quasisymmetric functions and the Shareshian-Wachs theorem relating Hessenberg variety point counts to chromatic quasisymmetric function evaluations. For general supports, develop combinatorial-algebraic tools showing the relevant Hall scalar products specialize to polynomials in q, potentially using geometric methods on Springer fibers and deformation arguments to reduce arbitrary supports to Hessenberg-type patterns.
